artifact: §11 — evaluator implementation audit of lib/contract-model/evaluation-v2/atomic-contract.ts (236 lines, read in full)
scope: the V3 derivation layer only. matching.ts and semantic-correspondence.ts are frozen upstream and were read for the surfacing question but not audited as V3 code.

checklist.item: creditEligibility is exactly matchStatus in {EXACT_SINGLE, EXACT_COMPOSITE}
checklist.evidence: CREDIT_STATUSES; deriveAtomicContract. No other branch can produce CREDIT.

checklist.item: no dataset-, package-, documentId- or section-specific branching
checklist.evidence: the module contains no dataset key, package name, documentId or sectionRef literal. Its only inputs are UnitEvaluationResult and a candidate map.

checklist.item: representationCompleteness FULL only for the two credit statuses, PARTIAL only for PARTIAL, else NONE
checklist.evidence: deriveRepresentationCompleteness; REPRESENTATION_FULL_STATUSES is an alias of CREDIT_STATUSES, so FULL and CREDIT cannot diverge.

checklist.item: verificationStatus never invents a verification event
checklist.evidence: deriveVerificationStatus returns NOT_EVALUATED when no matched candidate carries a verifierFinding, rather than NOT_VERIFIED or VERIFIED.

checklist.item: evidenceQuality is a pure re-expression of the frozen groundTruthQuality audit
checklist.evidence: deriveEvidenceQuality is a total switch over unit.groundTruthQuality with no other input.

checklist.item: dangerousSilentOmission uses the same CRITICAL/MATERIAL gate as the frozen dangerousUnaccountedV2
surfacingStatus is claim-specific — a candidate that does not correspond to this claim cannot surface it
checklist.evidence: deriveSurfacingStatus reuses unit.explicitlySurfacedAsUnsafe, which matching.ts computes only over `corresponding` = [...full, ...partial] (matching.ts lines 95-103). A non-corresponding candidate is structurally excluded, and the frozen I_CLAIM_IDENTITY dimension forces a sibling-anchored candidate to INDETERMINATE so it never reaches `corresponding`.

checklist.item: surfacingStatus requires the flag to cover the whole claim when the claim is composite
checklist.evidence: neither 02-atomic-contract-spec.json nor 05-operational-rubric.json states a coverage threshold for a composite claim. The implemented rule is: ANY corresponding claim-specific flag sets SPECIFICALLY_SURFACED for the whole claim. This is a defensible reading, not a contract violation. It is AMB-1 in 02-v3-contract-reconstruction.json and is the root of all 14 non-unanimous surfacing disagreements.

checklist.item: derivedDiagnosticLabel is diagnostic-only and never feeds a safety dimension
checklist.evidence: its result is written to the output object and read by nothing else; anyPairHasRole, the one non-claim-identity-filtered scan in the module, is called only from deriveDiagnosticLabel and is documented as such.

checklist.item: the module introduces no new matching logic
checklist.evidence: every field is a total function of already-computed UnitEvaluationResult fields plus a candidate lookup. No text comparison, no scoring, no thresholds.

checklist.item: outputs are deterministic for fixed input
checklist.evidence: no Date, no Math.random, no order-dependent iteration affecting a result. Empirically the 1,115-unit run reproduces byte-identically 23 days apart (artifact 07).

statement: No implementation defect was found. The one non-conformance is a non-conformance to a rule that does not exist: the contract is silent where the evaluator had to choose. That is a contract defect, not an evaluator defect.
